prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot to Shore Control Room), Main Transformer (loading/temp monitored, abnormal trend escalated; protection settings under separate approval), export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory to Grid Dispatcher if capability<dispatch target; Dispatcher sets permitted export; relay applies accepted ceiling, keeps protection unless authorized switching plan). Public grid, port out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; output target within protection; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms to Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace to Substation Operator). Substation Operator: switching, clearances after authorization. Control Engineer: one-action steps, hold points; verifies limit level/time/ramp; stepwise reduction; gradual restore after confirmed release; confirms software change purpose/scope. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint (Duty Planner records basis/actions/approvals/open checks for handover), Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarm priority safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt to Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale), Work Permit Portal (Isolation Boundary Sketch), Operations Radio Console, Warehouse System. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy, Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note to Duty Planner). Personnel counts per movement, vessel, location, at departure/arrival/intermediate points: Marine Coordinator sets expected count (Berth Slot Confirmation), confirms reconciliation before movements resume; Vessel Master verifies (Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction to Personnel Tracking Console, total updated only with reason); Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft counted independently; Service Operations Vessel (Recovery Basket Load Sheet); North/South Access Scanner record access. Unresolved discrepancies go to handover. Software lifecycle: owner, approved version, baseline (versions, parameters, dependencies, hardware); access-controlled repos;

New part:
S611: Operational handover records identify the deployed change, any outstanding limitations, and the responsible technical contact.
S612: Emergency arrangements define who may direct an incident, who supports rescue, and who may authorize a return to work.
S613: The Shore Control Room maintains the incident log and provides a single operational point of contact for offshore teams.
S614: The Rescue Coordinator leads rescue planning and coordinates requests for external assistance.
S615: The Field Supervisor directs personnel at the affected work site until control is formally transferred.
S616: The Vessel Master retains authority over vessel safety, navigation, and decisions to approach or withdraw from a casualty.
S617: The HSE Officer advises on personnel hazards, rescue procedures, and the use of emergency equipment.
S618: The Marine Coordinator maintains awareness of vessel locations, access constraints, and available marine support.
S619: The Personnel Tracking Console supports personnel accounting, but the incident lead verifies headcounts with the teams involved.
S620: Crew Transfer Vessel operations are suspended when sea conditions, visibility, or transfer arrangements exceed approved limits.
S621: A Daughter Craft may support a local response only when its crew, equipment, and launch conditions are suitable.
S622: A Service Operations Vessel may provide accommodation, medical support, and a stable platform when its position and capability permit.
S623: The Helideck is used for evacuation only when aviation conditions, deck readiness, and receiving arrangements are acceptable.
S624: The Weather Service provides forecast information for planning, while operational decisions account for observed local conditions.
S625: The Metocean Buoy provides site measurements that help assess whether a planned response remains feasible.
S626: The Weather Analyst interprets forecast uncertainty and communicates material changes to the Rescue Coordinator.
S627: The Operations Radio Console supports communications between the Shore Control Room, vessels, and offshore work teams.
S628: Emergency Generator readiness is checked as part of site emergency preparedness and restoration planning.
S629: The Fire Detection Panel provides alarm indications that responders use alongside direct reports from personnel on site.
S630: The Control Engineer supports remote shutdown actions when communications and equipment status allow safe intervention.
S631: Electrical recovery work requires qualified personnel, verified isolation, and a safe means of access before hands-on activity begins.
S632: Recovery of injured or incapacitated personnel may be delayed by vessel motion, limited access, lifting capacity, or deteriorating conditions.
S633: Offshore recovery plans identify the point at which continued response would expose rescuers to unacceptable risk.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
